claims.statement: The repository's default verification posture is CPU-first and offline: shared fixtures provide small attention and model configurations, while the data-pipeline module uses pytest.importorskip("shared_data") and therefore skips when the sibling package is unavailable.
The standard project validation ladder includes the full pytest suite, the analytical KV-cache benchmark, strict documentation-reference coverage, and documentation lint.

Attention regression coverage protects prefill sliding-window masking, sink causality, chunk-prefill alignment, GQA repetition, sink clamping, and the alternating even-windowed/odd-global layer contract.

MixedKVCache has distinct lifecycle and storage invariants: windowed layers retain an ordered recent ring-buffer view, global layers retain the complete prefix in insertion order, and reset empties both stores.

Generation tests treat no-cache replay as a correctness reference and require cached and no-cache one-token greedy generation to agree, while also checking output length and prompt-position helper behavior.

MoE correctness is defined by top-k in-range routing with normalized selected weights, always-on shared experts, deterministic stable dispatch, and an FP32-stable auxiliary load-balancing loss whose gradients reach the router and training objective.

The Triton execution contract requires a CPU-runnable pure-PyTorch reference plus GPU-gated kernel tests; explicit triton_grouped configuration must raise clear errors when unavailable or over hard caps and must not silently fall back.

ModelConfig validates shape, GQA divisibility, RoPE parity, expert-count, window, and YaRN invariants before construction, with warnings for odd-layer pruning and shorter evaluation context; model tests protect tied storage and unique parameter accounting.

Training verification covers schedule boundaries and monotonic decay, chunked cross-entropy equivalence and gradients, full-model gradients, gradient-checkpoint invocation cadence, and non-finite loss detection.
Checkpoint safety requires exact model restoration, complete-step discovery, atomic sibling temporary-file replacement without leaked partial files, and deduplication of tied safetensors storage.

Data verification covers atomic IO and state persistence, normalized hashing and quality filtering, EOS and vocabulary boundaries, shard writing and verification, manifest consistency, raw-byte and legacy shard loading, and a synthetic end-to-end pipeline; these checks are conditional on shared_data availability.

The KV-cache headline is a deterministic analytical BF16 byte calculation comparing six windowed layers capped at 128 tokens with six full layers at 131,072 tokens and checking a 1.8x threshold; it does not establish trained passkey quality.

The passkey target remains a pending trained-checkpoint measurement: passkey_eval.py requires a checkpoint, evaluates configured contexts and positions, and reports the 85% target separately from the analytical cache metric.

The GPU end-to-end smoke script is an explicit eight-step CUDA integration gate covering BF16 forward/backward, stacked-versus-Triton equivalence, training, checkpoint round-trip, cached generation, and YaRN extrapolation; it fails when no CUDA device is available rather than serving as a CPU pass.

Documentation is a CI-facing change contract: strict reference checking resolves file.py:Symbol anchors and enforces public-symbol coverage, check_docs validates links, paths, control characters, and stale patterns, and the docs deployment workflow builds the portal on documentation-related pushes.

The repository policy requires narrow quiet validation for changes, but configuration, attention, routing, checkpoint, or documentation boundary changes should escalate from focused tests to the full suite and the relevant GPU or documentation gates.
